requirements.statement: Increasing the text size up to at least 200% causes no loss of information, by one of the listed means.

citations.quote: l’augmentation de la taille des caractères jusqu’à 200 %, au moins, ne doit pas provoquer de perte d’information. Cette règle est-elle respectée selon une de ces conditions (hors cas particuliers) ?

routes.statement: No information is lost when the browser's text enlargement function is used.

citations.quote: Lors de l’utilisation de la fonction d’agrandissement du texte du navigateur ;

routes.statement: No information is lost when the browser's graphic zoom functions are used.

citations.quote: Lors de l’utilisation des fonctions de zoom graphique du navigateur ;

routes.statement: No information is lost when an interface component of the site that enlarges the text or zooms is used.

citations.quote: Lors de l’utilisation d’un composant d’interface propre au site permettant d’agrandir le texte ou de zoomer.

exceptions.statement: Captions burned into a video are exempt, since the user cannot customise them.

Les sous-titres incrustés dans une vidéo ;

exceptions.statement: Text inside a canvas element is exempt.

citations.quote: Le texte au sein d’une balise `<canvas>`.

rationale.text: The test accepts any one of three means of enlarging text to 200%: the browser's text enlargement, the browser's graphic zoom, or a component of the site. It exempts content the user cannot customise: captions burned into video, text in images, text in a canvas. A loss of information is judgment: text that is clipped, overlapped or pushed out of reach at 200% may or may not lose what it says, and whether a pattern of pixels is text in an image is judgment too. A fault could prove failure only if it showed a loss under all three means, and the third depends on finding and using a component of the site, which needs judgment and interaction. So no check can fault under every reading or decide the requirement, and the entry is none. No axe rule is tagged for this test. Applicability is judgment: the test applies to text the user can customise, and a page whose only text is in images or a canvas would be outside it, which code cannot tell for certain. Needs lists state, because the third means is a component the user operates. Rendering the page with enlarged text or at 200% zoom is not one of the listed prerequisites; it is reported as something the schema cannot express.
